source_text:
Πᾶς δὲ προφήτης ἀληθινὸς θέλων καθῆσθαι πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἄξιός ἐστι τῆς τροφῆς αὐτοῦ.
ὡσαύτως διδάσκαλος ἀληθινός ἐστιν ἄξιος καὶ αὐτὸς ὥσπερ ὁ ἐργάτης τῆς τροφῆς αὐτοῦ.
πᾶσαν οὖν ἀπαρχὴν γεννημάτων ληνοῦ καὶ ἅλωνος, βοῶν τε καὶ προβάτων λαβὼν δώσεις τὴν ἀπαρχὴν τοῖς προφήταις: αὐτοὶ γάρ εἰσιν οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς ὑμῶν.
ἐὰν δὲ μὴ ἔχητε προφήτην, δότε τοῖς πτωχοῖς.
ἐὰν σιτίαν ποιῇς, τὴν ἀπαρχὴν λαβὼν δὸς κατὰ τὴν ἐντολήν.
ὡσαύτως κεράμιον οἴνου ἡ ἐλαίου ἀνοίξας, τὴν ἀπαρχὴν λαβὼν δὸς τοῖς προφήταις:
ἀργυρίου δὲ καὶ ἱματισμοῦ καὶ παντὸς κτήματος λαβὼν τὴν ἀπαρχήν, ὡς ἄν σοι δόξῃ, δὸς κατὰ τὴν ἐντολήν.
thought_title: Support for true prophets and teachers
orientation: The anonymous author is giving community rules, now instructing how to support true prophets and teachers with first fruits.
pass_a_gloss: But every true prophet wishing to settle among you is worthy of his food. Likewise a true teacher is worthy, he too, just as the worker, of his food. Therefore every first fruit of produce of winepress and threshing floor, of oxen and of sheep, taking you shall give the first fruit to the prophets; for they are your high priests. But if you do not have a prophet, give to the poor. If you make a batch of dough, taking the first fruit give according to the commandment. Likewise a jar of wine or of oil opening, taking the first fruit give to the prophets; but of silver and of clothing and of every possession taking the first fruit, as it may seem good to you, give according to the commandment.

choices.why: Fixed glossary term for the portion of produce and goods given to prophets or the poor.
The verb means to sit down or remain, and with πρὸς ὑμᾶς it indicates taking up residence with the community, not merely sitting.
The concrete sense of sustenance or daily food fits the context of material support.
The phrase refers to preparing grain food or dough, and 'batch of dough' captures the concrete domestic action.

choices.english: as it may seem good to you
choices.why: This preserves the impersonal optative sense of discretion left to the giver.
The text identifies prophets as the community's high priests, and the literal rendering preserves the striking claim.

pass_b_english: Every true prophet who wants to settle among you deserves his food.
In the same way, a true teacher also deserves his food, just like a worker.
So take the first fruits of all the produce of your winepress and threshing floor, and of your cattle and sheep, and give them to the prophets, for they are your high priests.
If you have no prophet, give them to the poor.
If you make a batch of dough, take the first fruits and give them according to the commandment.
Likewise, when you open a jar of wine or oil, take the first fruits and give them to the prophets.
And take the first fruits of silver, clothing, and every possession, and give them according to the commandment, as it may seem good to you.

polish.changed: Clarified pronoun references and agricultural terms, made the sequence of instructions flow naturally for modern readers, and kept every claim and qualification intact.

notes.quote: first fruit of all the produce of the winepress and threshing floor
notes.why: Agricultural terms unfamiliar to modern readers are left undefined.
notes.fix: Add a footnote: winepress = place where grapes are pressed; threshing floor = grain‑separating area.
